note: Admin User Language forces a user's preferred_admin_langcode via hook_entity_presave(). Config admin_user_language.settings has two keys: default_language_to_assign (a langcode, or -1 = no preference, or preferred_langcode = mirror the user's own site language) and prevent_user_override (bool). Shipped defaults: -1 / false. With prevent_user_override FALSE the language is applied only to new users (isNew); with TRUE it is re-applied on every save AND the admin-language field is disabled on the user form. Settings form: admin_user_language.basic_form (/admin/config/admin_user_language/settings); permission 'administer admin interface language'. Medium cases set a known config (assign en / prevent override; and the preferred_langcode option) and read it back. Hard cases: (1) config-only force English + prevent override; (2) a runtime test that adds Dutch (nl), the agent forces nl + prevents override, and verify creates a throwaway user and confirms the presave hook set preferred_admin_langcode to nl, then removes the user and nl.

evals.prompt: On a multilingual Drupal site using the admin_user_language module, which configuration keys control the forced administration-pages language, and where is the settings form?
evals.expected_output: The admin_user_language.settings config has default_language_to_assign (the langcode to assign, or -1 for no preference, or preferred_langcode to mirror the user's site language) and prevent_user_override (bool). The settings form is at /admin/config/admin_user_language/settings (route admin_user_language.basic_form).

evals.prompt: In the admin_user_language module, what is the difference in behavior when 'Force language' (prevent_user_override) is off versus on?
evals.expected_output: Off (FALSE): the language is applied only when the user is new (isNew) - a soft default existing users can change. On (TRUE): it is re-applied on every user save and the administration-pages-language field is disabled on the user form so users cannot change it.

evals.prompt: Which user field does the admin_user_language module set, and through which hook does it do so?
evals.expected_output: It sets the user entity's preferred_admin_langcode field, via hook_entity_presave() (admin_user_language_entity_presave), on user create/update.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has the admin_user_language module configured with a specific policy. Inspect the live configuration and state which administration language is assigned to users and whether users are prevented from overriding it.
evals.expected_output: admin_user_language.settings has default_language_to_assign = en and prevent_user_override = true (users are forced to English and cannot override it). Read via drush cget admin_user_language.settings.

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's admin_user_language configuration: what is default_language_to_assign set to, and what does that particular value mean for a user's administration language?
evals.expected_output: default_language_to_assign is set to the special value 'preferred_langcode', which means each user's administration-pages language mirrors their own site (preferred) language rather than a fixed one. prevent_user_override is false.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the admin_user_language module so that every user's administration-pages language is forced to English (en) and users are not allowed to override it. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set admin_user_language.settings default_language_to_assign = 'en' and prevent_user_override = true (via the settings form or drush cset).

evals.prompt: This site has Dutch (nl) available as a language. Configure the admin_user_language module so that whenever a user is created or saved, their administration-pages language is forced to Dutch and they cannot override it. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set admin_user_language.settings default_language_to_assign = 'nl' and prevent_user_override = true. Verified by creating a new user and confirming hook_entity_presave set its preferred_admin_langcode to 'nl'.
